title: Association object (M:N with payload)
summary: Members ↔ projects where the link itself has data: role and joined_at.
description:
Members ↔ projects where the link itself has data: role and joined_at.

Why: A plain junction only says *that* two rows are linked. As soon as the link has attributes (role, date, grade, quantity) it becomes a model of its own — an association object — with a composite key and its own columns.
objectives: lab_memberships: member_id + project_id FKs (ON DELETE CASCADE), composite key
role (NOT NULL text) and joined_at (NOT NULL timestamp, default now())
hints: Model the junction as a class/model, not a bare secondary table.
The pair (member_id, project_id) is the key; role and joined_at are payload.
starterCode: // TODO: LabMember, LabProject and the association model LabMembership (lab_memberships)
why: A plain junction only says *that* two rows are linked. As soon as the link has attributes (role, date, grade, quantity) it becomes a model of its own — an association object — with a composite key and its own columns.
pitfalls: Using relationship(secondary=...) — there is nowhere to store the role.
Giving the junction a surrogate id and forgetting the composite UNIQUE.
teachAlong: Effect: the junction becomes an entity with a composite key.
Diagram: two FK arrows into lab_memberships plus its own columns.
mappingNotes: Compare your code with the Equivalent SQL panel. The gate introspects Postgres and runs rolled-back probe INSERTs.
solution:
model LabMember {
  id          Int             @id @default(autoincrement())
  name        String
  memberships LabMembership[]
  @@map("lab_members")
}

model LabProject {
  id          Int             @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  memberships LabMembership[]
  @@map("lab_projects")
}

model LabMembership {
  memberId  Int        @map("member_id")
  projectId Int        @map("project_id")
  role      String     @db.VarChar(40)
  joinedAt  DateTime   @default(now()) @map("joined_at")
  member    LabMember  @relation(fields: [memberId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  project   LabProject @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  @@id([memberId, projectId])
  @@map("lab_memberships")
}
